languages: regional languages (Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, Bengali, Kannada and more)
IN.privacy: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act)
IN.privacyNote: The DPDP Rules, 2025 are being phased in — forms need clear purpose-specific consent, and users must be able to withdraw it.
web: E-commerce sites must display seller details and a grievance officer under the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.
GST-compliant invoices (GSTIN, HSN/SAC codes) for paid orders.
RBI card-tokenisation and e-mandate rules apply to saved cards and subscriptions.

PK.privacy: No comprehensive data-protection act in force yet (a Personal Data Protection Bill has been drafted)
PK.privacyNote: We build to GDPR-style consent and data-minimisation by default so you are ready when national rules are finalised.
web: Urdu content needs right-to-left (RTL) layout and Nastaliq-friendly fonts.
The Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016 (PECA) governs online content and data misuse.

BD.privacyNote: The Act replaced a 2025 ordinance — consent is required for most processing, and some duties phase in over 18 months.
web: Bangla typography (Unicode, proper conjuncts) matters for readability and SEO.
Facebook-led "f-commerce" shops often need a proper website to scale beyond social selling.

LK.privacy: Personal Data Protection Act, No. 9 of 2022
LK.privacyNote: The Act is coming into force in phases; core duties (lawful processing, DPOs, breach notification) apply from 1 January 2027.
web: Trilingual content (Sinhala, Tamil, English) is common for public-facing sites.

KZ.privacy: Law on Personal Data and Their Protection (2013)
KZ.privacyNote: Personal data of Kazakh citizens generally has to be stored on servers located in Kazakhstan — hosting choice matters.
web: Bilingual Kazakh/Russian interfaces are expected; Kazakh is moving from Cyrillic to Latin script.
KZ.search: Google leads, but Yandex still has meaningful share — we check rankings on both.

UZ.privacyNote: Since 2021 personal data of Uzbek citizens must be stored on servers inside Uzbekistan.
web: Uzbek (Latin script) and Russian versions are usually both needed.
UZ.search: Google and Yandex are both used — Telegram is often the main customer channel.

AE.privacy: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection (PDPL)
AE.privacyNote: Free zones have their own regimes — DIFC Data Protection Law 2020 and ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021.
web: Bilingual Arabic/English sites need a true RTL layout, not a mirrored template.
Prices are usually shown VAT-inclusive (5% UAE VAT).

SA.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law (PDPL), enforced by SDAIA
SA.privacyNote: Full enforcement began in September 2024 — cross-border transfers and consent need to be documented.
web: Arabic-first RTL design is expected for consumer brands.
VAT-registered businesses must issue ZATCA-compliant e-invoices (FATOORA); VAT is 15%.

QA.privacy: Law No. 13 of 2016 on Personal Data Privacy Protection (PDPPL)
QA.privacyNote: Companies in the Qatar Financial Centre follow separate QFC data-protection regulations.
web: Arabic/English bilingual sites with RTL support are standard for public-facing brands.

KW.privacy: CITRA Data Privacy Protection Regulation (Resolution No. 26 of 2024)
KW.privacyNote: Kuwait has no general data-protection law; the regulation applies to CITRA-licensed telecom and online service providers, who must report breaches.
web: Arabic/English with RTL support; KWD prices use three decimal places.

BH.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 30 of 2018)
BH.privacyNote: Consent, purpose limitation and cross-border transfer rules apply to customer data.
web: Arabic/English sites with RTL; BHD prices use three decimal places.

OM.privacyNote: In force since February 2023 and fully enforceable since February 2026 — explicit consent is required before processing personal data.
web: Arabic/English with RTL; OMR prices use three decimal places.

JO.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law No. 24 of 2023
JO.privacyNote: The law introduces consent, data-subject rights and breach-notification duties for businesses.
web: Arabic/English with RTL support.

GB.privacy: UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018
GB.privacyNote: PECR governs cookies and e-marketing; the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 updates parts of both regimes.
web: Most non-essential cookies need prior consent under PECR; since February 2026 some analytics and preference cookies are exempt if users get clear information and an easy opt-out.
Online shops must follow the Consumer Contracts Regulations (14-day cancellation for most goods).
Limited companies must show their registered name and number on the website.

DE.privacy: GDPR and the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG)
DE.privacyNote: Cookies and tracking fall under the TDDDG; German regulators are strict about consent banners and US data transfers.
web: Every commercial site needs an Impressum (legal notice) under § 5 of the Digitale-Dienste-Gesetz (DDG).
The Barrierefreiheitsstärkungsgesetz (BFSG) brings accessibility duties for online shops from 28 June 2025.
Customers expect "Kauf auf Rechnung" (pay by invoice) and clear withdrawal (Widerruf) information.

FR.privacy: GDPR and the Loi Informatique et Libertés
FR.privacyNote: The CNIL actively fines non-compliant cookie banners — "Refuse all" must be as visible as "Accept all".
web: Mentions légales (legal notice) are mandatory on business websites.
Consumer-facing content should be available in French (Loi Toubon).
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

NL.privacy: GDPR and the Dutch GDPR Implementation Act (UAVG)
NL.privacyNote: The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens enforces cookie and tracking consent.
web: Cookie consent must be opt-in (ePrivacy rules) — rejecting has to be as easy as accepting.
Dutch shoppers expect iDEAL at checkout (being migrated to the European Wero wallet).
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

ES.privacyNote: The LSSI requires a legal notice (aviso legal) and consent for non-essential cookies.
web: Catalan versions help for Barcelona-focused brands.
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

IT.privacy: GDPR and the Italian Privacy Code (Legislative Decree 196/2003)
IT.privacyNote: The Garante’s cookie guidelines require granular consent and a clear way to refuse.
web: Electronic invoicing through the SdI system is mandatory for B2B and B2C invoices.
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

IE.privacy: GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018
IE.privacyNote: The Data Protection Commission is lead EU regulator for many global tech firms headquartered in Dublin.
web: Cookie consent must be opt-in (ePrivacy rules) — rejecting has to be as easy as accepting.
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

CH.privacy: Revised Federal Act on Data Protection (revFADP / nDSG)
CH.privacyNote: In force since 1 September 2023 — privacy notices must list recipients and countries data goes to.
web: Multilingual sites (DE/FR/IT) are expected for national reach.

SE.privacy: GDPR and the Swedish Data Protection Act (2018:218)
SE.privacyNote: IMY (the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection) supervises compliance.
web: Cookie consent must be opt-in (ePrivacy rules) — rejecting has to be as easy as accepting.
BankID is the standard for login and e-signing.
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

PL.privacy: GDPR and the Polish Act on the Protection of Personal Data (2018)
PL.privacyNote: UODO is the national supervisory authority.
web: KSeF national e-invoicing is mandatory since 2026 (February for large firms, April for others; the smallest taxpayers join in 2027).
The European Accessibility Act applies to many e-commerce and digital services from 28 June 2025 (WCAG 2.1 AA is the practical baseline).

US.privacy: State privacy laws (California CCPA/CPRA and a growing list of other states)
US.privacyNote: There is no single federal privacy law — COPPA covers children’s data, CAN-SPAM covers email and TCPA covers SMS.
web: ADA lawsuits make WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility a practical requirement for business sites.
Online sellers may owe sales tax in states where they have economic nexus.

CA.privacyNote: CASL requires express consent before sending commercial emails or SMS.
web: Québec requires French-language versions for consumer-facing content (Bill 96).
Ontario’s AODA sets web-accessibility duties for many organisations.

BR.privacy: LGPD (Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados, Law 13,709/2018)
BR.privacyNote: The ANPD enforces the LGPD — you need a legal basis for each use of customer data and a named data officer (encarregado).
web: Shoppers expect Pix, boleto and card instalments (parcelamento) at checkout.

MX.privacy: Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties (new LFPDPPP, in force since March 2025)
MX.privacyNote: A privacy notice (aviso de privacidad) is mandatory wherever you collect personal data.
web: Invoices must be issued as CFDI e-invoices through the SAT system.
Many customers pay in cash at OXXO or by SPEI bank transfer; card instalments (meses sin intereses) are common.

CO.privacy: Law 1581 of 2012 (Habeas Data) and Decree 1377 of 2013
CO.privacyNote: Larger companies must register their databases with the SIC’s national registry (RNBD).
web: DIAN electronic invoicing (facturación electrónica) applies to most sellers.

AR.privacyNote: The AAIP supervises data protection; databases with personal data must be registered.
web: Card instalments (cuotas) and Mercado Pago are expected at checkout; many B2B services quote in USD.

CL.privacy: Law 19,628 — being replaced by Law 21,719 (in force from December 2026)
CL.privacyNote: The new law creates a data-protection agency and GDPR-style duties, so new builds should plan for it now.
web: Electronic invoices and receipts (boleta electrónica) are issued through the SII.

SG.privacyNote: The PDPC requires breach notification, and marketing calls/SMS must respect the Do Not Call registry.
web: Mobile-first, fast sites are expected — Singapore has very high smartphone use.

JP.privacy: Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI)
JP.privacyNote: The PPC enforces the APPI, including rules on cross-border transfers and breach reporting.
web: Online sellers must publish a disclosure page under the Act on Specified Commercial Transactions (tokushōhō).
Japanese typography, dense information layouts and mobile performance strongly affect conversion.
JP.search: Google and Yahoo! JAPAN (which uses Google’s index) dominate — LINE is the main messaging channel.

MY.privacyNote: The 2024 amendments add mandatory breach notification, data-protection officers and data portability.
web: MyInvois e-invoicing is mandatory for businesses above the annual-sales threshold (RM3 million since September 2026).

TH.privacyNote: Fully enforced since June 2022 — consent and privacy notices are required for marketing data.
web: Thai-language typography and line-breaking need proper font and CSS handling.

ID.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law (Law No. 27 of 2022, UU PDP)
ID.privacyNote: The transition period ended in October 2024 — businesses must now comply in full.
web: Bahasa Indonesia content is essential for local search visibility.

VN.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law (No. 91/2025/QH15) and Decree 356/2025, both effective 1 January 2026
VN.privacyNote: Consent and impact assessments are required, and some cross-border transfers must be documented.
web: Vietnamese diacritics need full font support for readability and SEO.

KR.privacyNote: PIPA is one of the strictest privacy laws in Asia — separate consents are often needed for marketing and third-party sharing.
web: Korean payment flows run through local PG providers rather than global gateways alone.
KR.search: Naver is a major search portal alongside Google — SEO plans should include Naver Search Advisor.

ZA.privacyNote: The Information Regulator expects a registered information officer and documented consent for direct marketing.
web: The ECT Act requires suppliers selling online to disclose key business and pricing details.
Fast, lightweight pages matter — many users browse on prepaid mobile data.

NG.privacyNote: The NDPC oversees compliance; larger data controllers have registration and audit duties.
web: Bank transfer is a primary checkout method, so gateways with transfer support convert better.
Lightweight pages matter — many users browse on mobile data.

KE.privacyNote: Most data controllers and processors must register with the Office of the Data Protection Commissioner (ODPC); very small entities outside listed sectors are exempt.
web: M-Pesa integration (Daraja API / Lipa na M-Pesa) is usually essential for online payments.
KRA eTIMS e-invoicing applies to most businesses.

EG.privacy: Personal Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020
EG.privacyNote: Executive Regulations were issued in late 2025 — consent, data-subject rights and licensing for some processing and transfers apply.
web: Arabic RTL with Egyptian-Arabic copy for consumer brands; English for B2B.

AU.privacy: Privacy Act 1988 (Australian Privacy Principles), amended in 2024
AU.privacyNote: The Spam Act 2003 requires consent and an unsubscribe option for marketing email and SMS.
web: Prices shown to consumers must include GST (10%).
The Disability Discrimination Act makes WCAG accessibility a practical requirement.

NZ.privacyNote: Serious breaches must be reported to the Privacy Commissioner, and since May 2026 (IPP 3A) people must be told when their data is collected indirectly.
web: Consumer prices are shown GST-inclusive (15%).

Clear usage limits so AI costs stay predictable

Monthly reporting on clicks, leads and rankings
